message.content: Read redu.md and deploy Memos on redu.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

Use when invoking models, setting up Knowledge Bases, creating agents, applying guardrails, deploying to AgentCore, troubleshooting Bedrock errors (ThrottlingException, AccessDeniedException), or choosing models (Claude, Llama, [infra], Titan). ALSO USE for prompt caching setup and debugging, quota health checks and throttling diagnosis, cost attribution and tracking, migrating between Claude model generations (4.5 to 4.6 to 4.7), chunking strategies, API selection (Converse vs InvokeModel), guardrail capabilities, and model selection. Also covers AgentCore Payments setup (x402, microtransactions, Payment Manager, Connector, Instrument, Coinbase CDP, Stripe Privy, 402 Payment Required, pay for content, paid endpoint, agent payments). NOT for custom model training, Rekognition, or Comprehend.

Also covers AWS Blocks topics with validated, version-specific patterns that prevent common mistakes. Triggers when user mentions AWS Blocks; project has aws-blocks/ directory; code imports @aws-blocks packages.

Use when deploying, debugging, or optimizing containers on AWS. ALSO USE for container deployment options (ECS vs ECS Express Mode), networking modes, health check troubleshooting, OOM errors, secrets injection, blue/green deployments, ECR image management, and App Runner sunset guidance and migration. NOT for Kubernetes, EKS, or CI/CD pipelines.

Covers Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon MQ, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Data Firehose, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, and Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK). Use when implementing messaging and streaming patterns.

Covers Log Insights queries, alarms (metric, composite, anomaly), dashboards, custom metrics/EMF, X-Ray tracing and sampling, ADOT collector config, CloudTrail auditing, and end-to-end Application Signals enablement via ADOT SDKs (CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on, CloudWatch Agent IAM, OTLP endpoints, ServiceEvents, Dynamic Instrumentation), breakpoint and snapshot in Dynamic Instrumentation, live data capture in running service, debug without redeploying. Applies to CloudWatch, alarms, dashboards, EMF, X-Ray, traces, CloudTrail,  ADOT, monitoring, synthetics/canaries, OR enabling/onboarding/instrumenting a service for Application Signals. Not for app logging or security threat detection.
- aws-sdk-js-v3-usage: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 development patterns. Use when writing JavaScript or TypeScript code that uses AWS services via @aws-sdk/* packages (aws-sdk-js-v3), or when asked about schemas, runtime validation, serialization, or code generation in the context of the JS/TS AWS SDK.
- aws-sdk-python-usage: AWS SDK for Python (boto3/botocore) development patterns. You MUST use this skill when writing Python code that uses AWS services via boto3 or botocore. This includes creating service clients or resources, configuring sessions and credentials, handling errors with ClientError, using paginators and waiters, S3 file transfers and presigned URLs, DynamoDB table operations, and any boto3/botocore client configuration. Use this skill whenever Python code imports boto3 or botocore, or when the user asks about AWS operations in Python.
- aws-sdk-swift-usage: AWS SDK for Swift development patterns. Use when writing Swift code that uses AWS services via aws-sdk-swift package.
- aws-serverless: Builds, deploys, manages, debugs, configures, and optimizes serverless applications on AWS using Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, EventBridge, and SAM/CDK. Covers cold starts, CORS debugging, event source mappings, troubleshooting, concurrency, SnapStart, Powertools, function URLs, EventBridge Scheduler, Lambda layers, and production readiness. Triggers on mentions of Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, SAM templates, CDK serverless stacks, DynamoDB stream triggers, SQS event sources, cold starts, timeouts, 502/504 errors, throttling, concurrency, CORS, Powertools, or any event-driven architecture on AWS, even without the word "serverless." Activates when a developer needs to authenticate to AWS for local development, when an AWS operation fails due to missing or expired credentials, or when someone asks about setting up AWS access. Triggers: "set up AWS", "configure AWS", "aws login", "get credentials", "authenticate", "session expired", "token expired", "no credentials", "AccessDeniedException" with no configured credentials.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). content.content:
1	---
2	redu_schema: 2
3	repo: https://github.com/usememos/memos
4	plan:
5	  tool: deploy_compose
6	  image: neosmemo/memos:0.30.0
7	  port: 5230
8	  vm: m1.small
9	  flavor_id: "2"
10	  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
11	  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0348
12	bootstrap:
13	  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
14	  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
15	  source: memos
16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔ neosmemo/memos:latest DOES NOT EXIST. The Docker Hub API returns 404 for that tag, while ghcr.io/usememos/memos:latest does exist, so a habit-written :latest reference fails to pull from one registry and succeeds on the other. Both registries receive the same digests from the same release job, so either is fine as long as you PIN A VERSION: neosmemo/memos:0.30.0 was current on 2026-08-16. Pinning also stops a redeploy crossing a release with a breaking default, which v0.30.0 itself had."
18	  - "⛔⛔ THE FIRST ACCOUNT TO SIGN UP BECOMES ADMIN, AND SIGNUP IS OPEN BY DEFAULT. Verified in server/router/api/v1/user_service.go:200-235: when no users exist, the account being created is assigned the admin role, and acl_config.go puts CreateUser in the anonymous-reachable set with DisallowUserRegistration defaulting to false. There is no setup lock and no bootstrap token in v0.30.0. So between the container going healthy and you creating your account, whoever loads the sign-up page first owns the instance. Create the account IMMEDIATELY, or better, ship the provisioning file described in the next quirk so registration is closed before the hostname is ever reachable."
19	  - "CLOSE REGISTRATION AT DEPLOY TIME, NOT AFTERWARDS. Mount a file at /etc/secrets/memos-instance-setting-general.json containing {\"key\":\"GENERAL\",\"generalSetting\":{\"disallowUserRegistration\":true}}. Per the v0.30.0 release notes this makes the setting read-only in both the UI and the API until the file is removed, which is stronger than a toggle someone can flip back. Then create the admin account yourself. If the user wants open signup, that is a deliberate choice to make with them, not a default to leave in place."
20	  - "⛔ MEMOS_INSTANCE_URL IS A TWO-WAY TRAP, and this is the decision to put to the user rather than guess. Leave it UNSET and the instance is private: RSS returns early (server/router/rss/rss.go:73,116), /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml return 404, anonymous avatar and public-attachment serving is blocked, CORS loses the trusted origin, and e-mail notification links have no base URL. SET it and anonymous ListMemos and GetMemo become permitted, so every memo marked PUBLIC is world-readable and a sitemap of all of them is served. Neither is wrong; they are different products. Ask which one they want, say what you set, and never set it silently just to make RSS work."
21	  - "⛔ DATABASE: set MEMOS_DRIVER=postgres AND MEMOS_DSN, or it silently uses SQLite. The driver defaults to sqlite (cmd/memos/main.go:122,130) with the file at /var/opt/memos/memos_prod.db, so a deploy that forgets the driver comes up perfectly healthy and loses every memo, every account and every access token on the next VM replacement. Only sqlite, mysql and postgres are accepted; anything else is a hard 'unknown db driver' error, which is at least loud. Memos does NOT read redu's injected PG* variables individually: build the DSN yourself from them."
22	  - "SET sslmode EXPLICITLY IN THE DSN. The DSN goes straight to lib/pq, whose default sslmode is `require`, which means encrypted but with the certificate NOT verified (lib/pq connector.go:60-61). Over redu's private network that is survivable; it is still worth being deliberate. Build it as postgres://${PGUSER}:[REDACTED:conn-password]@${PGHOST}:${PGPORT}/${PGDATABASE}?sslmode=require and say in the handover which mode you chose and why. There is also a MEMOS_DSN_FILE variant read by their entrypoint; setting both MEMOS_DSN and MEMOS_DSN_FILE is a hard exit."
23	  - "⛔ THE VOLUME IS STILL REQUIRED WITH POSTGRES. This is the one people get wrong after wiring the database correctly. Attachments default to LOCAL storage under /var/opt/memos/assets/ regardless of the driver (store/instance_setting.go:306-310), and .thumbnail_cache and .motion_cache live beside them. Postgres holds the memos; the files attached to them do not. Mount a volume on /var/opt/memos or every upload disappears on the next redeploy while the notes referencing them survive."
24	  - "PORT 5230, from the image env, NOT the binary default. scripts/Dockerfile sets MEMOS_PORT=5230 and exposes it, while the binary's own default is 8081. Pass 5230 to deploy_compose. Health probe: GET /healthz."
25	  - "MEMOS_MODE DOES NOT EXIST in v0.30.0 and setting it does nothing. It appears in old tutorials and in their own test harness. The real keys are demo, addr, port, unix-sock, data, driver, dsn, instance-url, allow-private-webhooks and log-level, each read as MEMOS_<KEY>. Do not carry MEMOS_MODE=prod forward from a blog post and assume it did something."
26	  - "LEAVE MEMOS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_WEBHOOKS AT FALSE. Turning it on lets any user point a webhook at addresses on the private network, which turns the instance into an SSRF probe inside the user's own infrastructure. It defaults to false; keep it there unless the user asks and understands. MEMOS_DEMO must stay false too."
27	  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. The app runs its own migrations at boot and detects a fresh database by probing for the memo table."
28	  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE, AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO NUMBER. It is a statically linked Go binary on alpine with no interpreter or JVM, so m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) is a reasonable floor and makes this the cheapest entry in the library. The two things that will actually move memory are the 30 MB default per-upload limit and server-side thumbnail and motion transcoding, so a user storing a lot of media should be on m1.medium. Measure it on your run and write the number back rather than repeating this paragraph."
29	  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.035/hr, roughly GBP 25 a month; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2', port 5230."
30	  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
31	  - "LICENCE: plain MIT, verified from LICENSE:1-21, with no addendum, no Commons Clause and no network clause. Nothing to reason about for a self-hoster. The only obligation is retaining the notice; MIT grants no trademark rights, so do not rebrand and redistribute under the Memos name."
32	  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. The admin password and the DSN both belong to the user. Hand them over in the session; the deploy log records that registration was closed and an admin exists, never the values."
33	  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back. The measured memory figure is the most useful thing your run can add, since upstream publishes none."
34	  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, ON PURPOSE. delete_deployment removes the app VM but keeps the managed Postgres so the notes survive, and that DB keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. ⚠️ The ATTACHMENTS live on the app VM's volume, so they go with the deployment while the notes referencing them survive. Say that plainly before deleting."
35	---
36	
37	# Self-host Memos on redu
38	
39	A fast, private place for notes and short posts: one small Go container, a managed Postgres beside
40	it, a public HTTPS URL. The cheapest entry in this library, at roughly GBP 25 a month.
41	
42	## What this deploys
43	
44	- **Memos** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.small VM, port 5230.
45	- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so your notes survive every redeploy.
46	- A volume on `/var/opt/memos`, which holds your attachments.
47	- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.
48	
49	About GBP 0.035/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.
50	
51	## Deploy
52	
53	Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
54	directory containing this file:
55	
56	    Read redu.md and deploy Memos on redu.
57	
58	The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.
59	
60	## One decision to make before you deploy
61	
62	**Private, or publicly readable?** Memos decides this with a single variable, and it swings both
63	ways:
64	
65	- **Leave `MEMOS_INSTANCE_URL` unset** and the instance is private. RSS, the sitemap,
66	  `robots.txt` and anonymous attachment links all stop working.
67	- **Set it** and RSS and public links work, but every memo you mark PUBLIC becomes readable by
68	  anyone, and a sitemap listing them is served.
69	
70	Neither is wrong. They are different products. Decide before you deploy rather than discovering
71	it afterwards.
72	
73	## The three that actually break it
74	
75	**The signup race.** The first account created becomes the admin, and registration is open by
76	default, with no setup lock. Between the container going healthy and you signing up, whoever
77	finds the URL owns the instance. The recipe closes registration with a provisioning file *before*
78	the hostname resolves.
79	
80	**The driver.** Without `MEMOS_DRIVER=postgres` it quietly uses SQLite inside the container. It
81	comes up healthy and loses everything on the next redeploy.
82	
83	**The volume.** Even with Postgres wired correctly, attachments still go to local disk. Postgres
84	keeps your notes; without a volume the files attached to them vanish.
85	
86	## Deploy log
87	
88	- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
89	  hourly rate, and should record actual memory use, since upstream publishes no figure at all.
90

# Self-host Memos on redu

A fast, private place for notes and short posts: one small Go container, a managed Postgres beside
it, a public HTTPS URL. The cheapest entry in this library, at roughly GBP 25 a month.

## What this deploys

- **Memos** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.small VM, port 5230.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so your notes survive every redeploy.
- A volume on `/var/opt/memos`, which holds your attachments.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.035/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Memos on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## One decision to make before you deploy

**Private, or publicly readable?** Memos decides this with a single variable, and it swings both
ways:

- **Leave `MEMOS_INSTANCE_URL` unset** and the instance is private. RSS, the sitemap,
  `robots.txt` and anonymous attachment links all stop working.
- **Set it** and RSS and public links work, but every memo you mark PUBLIC becomes readable by
  anyone, and a sitemap listing them is served.

Neither is wrong. They are different products. Decide before you deploy rather than discovering
it afterwards.

## The three that actually break it

**The signup race.** The first account created becomes the admin, and registration is open by
default, with no setup lock. Between the container going healthy and you signing up, whoever
finds the URL owns the instance. The recipe closes registration with a provisioning file *before*
the hostname resolves.

**The driver.** Without `MEMOS_DRIVER=postgres` it quietly uses SQLite inside the container. It
comes up healthy and loses everything on the next redeploy.

**The volume.** Even with Postgres wired correctly, attachments still go to local disk. Postgres
keeps your notes; without a volume the files attached to them vanish.

## Deploy log

- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
  hourly rate, and should record actual memory use, since upstream publishes no figure at all.

redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/usememos/memos
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: neosmemo/memos:0.30.0
  port: 5230
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"

  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0348
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: memos
quirks:
  - "⛔ neosmemo/memos:latest DOES NOT EXIST. The Docker Hub API returns 404 for that tag, while ghcr.io/usememos/memos:latest does exist, so a habit-written :latest reference fails to pull from one registry and succeeds on the other. Both registries receive the same digests from the same release job, so either is fine as long as you PIN A VERSION: neosmemo/memos:0.30.0 was current on 2026-08-16. Pinning also stops a redeploy crossing a release with a breaking default, which v0.30.0 itself had."
  - "⛔⛔ THE FIRST ACCOUNT TO SIGN UP BECOMES ADMIN, AND SIGNUP IS OPEN BY DEFAULT. Verified in server/router/api/v1/user_service.go:200-235: when no users exist, the account being created is assigned the admin role, and acl_config.go puts CreateUser in the anonymous-reachable set with DisallowUserRegistration defaulting to false. There is no setup lock and no bootstrap token in v0.30.0. So between the container going healthy and you creating your account, whoever loads the sign-up page first owns the instance. Create the account IMMEDIATELY, or better, ship the provisioning file described in the next quirk so registration is closed before the hostname is ever reachable."
  - "CLOSE REGISTRATION AT DEPLOY TIME, NOT AFTERWARDS. Mount a file at /etc/secrets/memos-instance-setting-general.json containing {\"key\":\"GENERAL\",\"generalSetting\":{\"disallowUserRegistration\":true}}. Per the v0.30.0 release notes this makes the setting read-only in both the UI and the API until the file is removed, which is stronger than a toggle someone can flip back. Then create the admin account yourself. If the user wants open signup, that is a deliberate choice to make with them, not a default to leave in place."
  - "⛔ MEMOS_INSTANCE_URL IS A TWO-WAY TRAP, and this is the decision to put to the user rather than guess. Leave it UNSET and the instance is private: RSS returns early (server/router/rss/rss.go:73,116), /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml return 404, anonymous avatar and public-attachment serving is blocked, CORS loses the trusted origin, and e-mail notification links have no base URL. SET it and anonymous ListMemos and GetMemo become permitted, so every memo marked PUBLIC is world-readable and a sitemap of all of them is served. Neither is wrong; they are different products. Ask which one they want, say what you set, and never set it silently just to make RSS work."
  - "⛔ DATABASE: set MEMOS_DRIVER=postgres AND MEMOS_DSN, or it silently uses SQLite. The driver defaults to sqlite (cmd/memos/main.go:122,130) with the file at /var/opt/memos/memos_prod.db, so a deploy that forgets the driver comes up perfectly healthy and loses every memo, every account and every access token on the next VM replacement. Only sqlite, mysql and postgres are accepted; anything else is a hard 'unknown db driver' error, which is at least loud. Memos does NOT read redu's injected PG* variables individually: build the DSN yourself from them."
  - "SET sslmode EXPLICITLY IN THE DSN. The DSN goes straight to lib/pq, whose default sslmode is `require`, which means encrypted but with the certificate NOT verified (lib/pq connector.go:60-61). Over redu's private network that is survivable; it is still worth being deliberate. Build it as postgres://${PGUSER}:[REDACTED:conn-password]@${PGHOST}:${PGPORT}/${PGDATABASE}?sslmode=require and say in the handover which mode you chose and why. There is also a MEMOS_DSN_FILE variant read by their entrypoint; setting both MEMOS_DSN and MEMOS_DSN_FILE is a hard exit."
  - "⛔ THE VOLUME IS STILL REQUIRED WITH POSTGRES. This is the one people get wrong after wiring the database correctly. Attachments default to LOCAL storage under /var/opt/memos/assets/ regardless of the driver (store/instance_setting.go:306-310), and .thumbnail_cache and .motion_cache live beside them. Postgres holds the memos; the files attached to them do not. Mount a volume on /var/opt/memos or every upload disappears on the next redeploy while the notes referencing them survive."
  - "PORT 5230, from the image env, NOT the binary default. scripts/Dockerfile sets MEMOS_PORT=5230 and exposes it, while the binary's own default is 8081. Pass 5230 to deploy_compose. Health probe: GET /healthz."
  - "MEMOS_MODE DOES NOT EXIST in v0.30.0 and setting it does nothing. It appears in old tutorials and in their own test harness. The real keys are demo, addr, port, unix-sock, data, driver, dsn, instance-url, allow-private-webhooks and log-level, each read as MEMOS_<KEY>. Do not carry MEMOS_MODE=prod forward from a blog post and assume it did something."
  - "LEAVE MEMOS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_WEBHOOKS AT FALSE. Turning it on lets any user point a webhook at addresses on the private network, which turns the instance into an SSRF probe inside the user's own infrastructure. It defaults to false; keep it there unless the user asks and understands. MEMOS_DEMO must stay false too."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. The app runs its own migrations at boot and detects a fresh database by probing for the memo table."
  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE, AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO NUMBER. It is a statically linked Go binary on alpine with no interpreter or JVM, so m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) is a reasonable floor and makes this the cheapest entry in the library. The two things that will actually move memory are the 30 MB default per-upload limit and server-side thumbnail and motion transcoding, so a user storing a lot of media should be on m1.medium. Measure it on your run and write the number back rather than repeating this paragraph."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.035/hr, roughly GBP 25 a month; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2', port 5230."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."

  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. The admin password and the DSN both belong to the user. Hand them over in the session; the deploy log records that registration was closed and an admin exists, never the values."
  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back. The measured memory figure is the most useful thing your run can add, since upstream publishes none."
  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, ON PURPOSE. delete_deployment removes the app VM but keeps the managed Postgres so the notes survive, and that DB keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. ⚠️ The ATTACHMENTS live on the app VM's volume, so they go with the deployment while the notes referencing them survive. Say that plainly before deleting."
---

# Self-host Memos on redu

A fast, private place for notes and short posts: one small Go container, a managed Postgres beside
it, a public HTTPS URL. The cheapest entry in this library, at roughly GBP 25 a month.

## What this deploys

- **Memos** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.small VM, port 5230.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so your notes survive every redeploy.
- A volume on `/var/opt/memos`, which holds your attachments.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.035/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Memos on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## One decision to make before you deploy

**Private, or publicly readable?** Memos decides this with a single variable, and it swings both
ways:

- **Leave `MEMOS_INSTANCE_URL` unset** and the instance is private. RSS, the sitemap,
  `robots.txt` and anonymous attachment links all stop working.
- **Set it** and RSS and public links work, but every memo you mark PUBLIC becomes readable by
  anyone, and a sitemap listing them is served.

Neither is wrong. They are different products. Decide before you deploy rather than discovering
it afterwards.

## The three that actually break it

**The signup race.** The first account created becomes the admin, and registration is open by
default, with no setup lock. Between the container going healthy and you signing up, whoever
finds the URL owns the instance. The recipe closes registration with a provisioning file *before*
the hostname resolves.

**The driver.** Without `MEMOS_DRIVER=postgres` it quietly uses SQLite inside the container. It
comes up healthy and loses everything on the next redeploy.

**The volume.** Even with Postgres wired correctly, attachments still go to local disk. Postgres
keeps your notes; without a volume the files attached to them vanish.

## Deploy log

- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
  hourly rate, and should record actual memory use, since upstream publishes no figure at all.

structuredContent.redu_md_markdown:
---
last_deploy:
  id: 428
  date: 2026-08-16
  status: ready
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/usememos/memos
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: neosmemo/memos:0.30.0
  port: 5230
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0348
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: memos
quirks:
  - "⛔ neosmemo/memos:latest DOES NOT EXIST. The Docker Hub API returns 404 for that tag, while ghcr.io/usememos/memos:latest does exist, so a habit-written :latest reference fails to pull from one registry and succeeds on the other. Both registries receive the same digests from the same release job, so either is fine as long as you PIN A VERSION: neosmemo/memos:0.30.0 was current on 2026-08-16. Pinning also stops a redeploy crossing a release with a breaking default, which v0.30.0 itself had."
  - "⛔⛔ THE FIRST ACCOUNT TO SIGN UP BECOMES ADMIN, AND SIGNUP IS OPEN BY DEFAULT. Verified in server/router/api/v1/user_service.go:200-235: when no users exist, the account being created is assigned the admin role, and acl_config.go puts CreateUser in the anonymous-reachable set with DisallowUserRegistration defaulting to false. There is no setup lock and no bootstrap token in v0.30.0. So between the container going healthy and you creating your account, whoever loads the sign-up page first owns the instance. Create the account IMMEDIATELY, or better, ship the provisioning file described in the next quirk so registration is closed before the hostname is ever reachable."
  - "CLOSE REGISTRATION AT DEPLOY TIME, NOT AFTERWARDS. Mount a file at /etc/secrets/memos-instance-setting-general.json containing {\"key\":\"GENERAL\",\"generalSetting\":{\"disallowUserRegistration\":true}}. Per the v0.30.0 release notes this makes the setting read-only in both the UI and the API until the file is removed, which is stronger than a toggle someone can flip back. Then create the admin account yourself. If the user wants open signup, that is a deliberate choice to make with them, not a default to leave in place."
  - "⛔ MEMOS_INSTANCE_URL IS A TWO-WAY TRAP, and this is the decision to put to the user rather than guess. Leave it UNSET and the instance is private: RSS returns early (server/router/rss/rss.go:73,116), /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml return 404, anonymous avatar and public-attachment serving is blocked, CORS loses the trusted origin, and e-mail notification links have no base URL. SET it and anonymous ListMemos and GetMemo become permitted, so every memo marked PUBLIC is world-readable and a sitemap of all of them is served. Neither is wrong; they are different products. Ask which one they want, say what you set, and never set it silently just to make RSS work."
  - "⛔ DATABASE: set MEMOS_DRIVER=postgres AND MEMOS_DSN, or it silently uses SQLite. The driver defaults to sqlite (cmd/memos/main.go:122,130) with the file at /var/opt/memos/memos_prod.db, so a deploy that forgets the driver comes up perfectly healthy and loses every memo, every account and every access token on the next VM replacement. Only sqlite, mysql and postgres are accepted; anything else is a hard 'unknown db driver' error, which is at least loud. Memos does NOT read redu's injected PG* variables individually: build the DSN yourself from them."
  - "SET sslmode EXPLICITLY IN THE DSN. The DSN goes straight to lib/pq, whose default sslmode is `require`, which means encrypted but with the certificate NOT verified (lib/pq connector.go:60-61). Over redu's private network that is survivable; it is still worth being deliberate. Build it as postgres://${PGUSER}:[REDACTED:conn-password]@${PGHOST}:${PGPORT}/${PGDATABASE}?sslmode=require and say in the handover which mode you chose and why. There is also a MEMOS_DSN_FILE variant read by their entrypoint; setting both MEMOS_DSN and MEMOS_DSN_FILE is a hard exit."
  - "⛔ THE VOLUME IS STILL REQUIRED WITH POSTGRES. This is the one people get wrong after wiring the database correctly. Attachments default to LOCAL storage under /var/opt/memos/assets/ regardless of the driver (store/instance_setting.go:306-310), and .thumbnail_cache and .motion_cache live beside them. Postgres holds the memos; the files attached to them do not. Mount a volume on /var/opt/memos or every upload disappears on the next redeploy while the notes referencing them survive."
  - "PORT 5230, from the image env, NOT the binary default. scripts/Dockerfile sets MEMOS_PORT=5230 and exposes it, while the binary's own default is 8081. Pass 5230 to deploy_compose. Health probe: GET /healthz."
  - "MEMOS_MODE DOES NOT EXIST in v0.30.0 and setting it does nothing. It appears in old tutorials and in their own test harness. The real keys are demo, addr, port, unix-sock, data, driver, dsn, instance-url, allow-private-webhooks and log-level, each read as MEMOS_<KEY>. Do not carry MEMOS_MODE=prod forward from a blog post and assume it did something."
  - "LEAVE MEMOS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_WEBHOOKS AT FALSE. Turning it on lets any user point a webhook at addresses on the private network, which turns the instance into an SSRF probe inside the user's own infrastructure. It defaults to false; keep it there unless the user asks and understands. MEMOS_DEMO must stay false too."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. The app runs its own migrations at boot and detects a fresh database by probing for the memo table."

# Self-host Memos on redu

A fast, private place for notes and short posts: one small Go container, a managed Postgres beside
it, a public HTTPS URL. The cheapest entry in this library, at roughly GBP 25 a month.

## What this deploys

- **Memos** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.small VM, port 5230.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so your notes survive every redeploy.
- A volume on `/var/opt/memos`, which holds your attachments.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.035/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Memos on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## One decision to make before you deploy

**Private, or publicly readable?** Memos decides this with a single variable, and it swings both
ways:

- **Leave `MEMOS_INSTANCE_URL` unset** and the instance is private. RSS, the sitemap,
  `robots.txt` and anonymous attachment links all stop working.
- **Set it** and RSS and public links work, but every memo you mark PUBLIC becomes readable by
  anyone, and a sitemap listing them is served.

Neither is wrong. They are different products. Decide before you deploy rather than discovering
it afterwards.

## The three that actually break it

**The signup race.** The first account created becomes the admin, and registration is open by
default, with no setup lock. Between the container going healthy and you signing up, whoever
finds the URL owns the instance. The recipe closes registration with a provisioning file *before*
the hostname resolves.

**The driver.** Without `MEMOS_DRIVER=postgres` it quietly uses SQLite inside the container. It
comes up healthy and loses everything on the next redeploy.

**The volume.** Even with Postgres wired correctly, attachments still go to local disk. Postgres
keeps your notes; without a volume the files attached to them vanish.

## Deploy log

- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
  hourly rate, and should record actual memory use, since upstream publishes no figure at all.
- 2026-08-16 deploy #428: ready, https://memos-q7v4m2xk.redu.cloud.

The two things that will actually move memory are the 30 MB default per-upload limit and server-side thumbnail and motion transcoding, so a user storing a lot of media should be on m1.medium. # Self-host Memos on redu

A fast, private place for notes and short posts: one small Go container, a managed Postgres beside
it, a public HTTPS URL. The cheapest entry in this library, at roughly GBP 25 a month.

## What this deploys

- **Memos** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.small VM, port 5230.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so your notes survive every redeploy.
- A volume on `/var/opt/memos`, which holds your attachments.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.035/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Memos on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## One decision to make before you deploy

**Private, or publicly readable?** Memos decides this with a single variable, and it swings both
ways:

- **Leave `MEMOS_INSTANCE_URL` unset** and the instance is private. RSS, the sitemap,
  `robots.txt` and anonymous attachment links all stop working.
- **Set it** and RSS and public links work, but every memo you mark PUBLIC becomes readable by
  anyone, and a sitemap listing them is served.

Neither is wrong. They are different products. Decide before you deploy rather than discovering
it afterwards.

Worth knowing, since "publicly readable" sounds worse than it is: public mode exposes only the
memos you explicitly mark PUBLIC. Measured on deploy #428, a PRIVATE memo fetched anonymously
still returned 401.

## The three that actually break it

**The signup race.** The first account created becomes the admin, and registration is open by
default, with no setup lock. Between the container going healthy and you signing up, whoever
finds the URL owns the instance. The recipe closes registration with a provisioning file before
the hostname resolves — **but deploy #428 measured that this is not sufficient on its own.** While
no admin exists, the first-account path bypasses the registration lock: an anonymous
`POST /api/v1/users` still succeeded and came back with `"role":"ADMIN"`. The identical call after
an admin existed was refused with `403 user registration is not allowed`. So the file protects the
second account onward. **You still have to claim the admin seat immediately**, then confirm
`needsSetup:false` before handing the URL to anyone.

**The driver.** Without `MEMOS_DRIVER=postgres` it quietly uses SQLite inside the container. It
comes up healthy and loses everything on the next redeploy. One command proves which one you got:
`docker exec <container> ls -la /var/opt/memos/` must be empty. A `memos_prod.db` sitting there is
the fallback.

**The volume.** Even with Postgres wired correctly, attachments still go to local disk. Postgres
keeps your notes; without a volume the files attached to them vanish.

## Deploy log

- 2026-08-16 deploy #428: ready, https://memos-q7v4m2xk.redu.cloud. **~3m50s** from the
  `deploy_compose` call to the first HTTP 200 on `/healthz`; the compose phase itself was **76s**
  (image pull, volume create, container start). m1.small app VM + managed Postgres m1.small,
  **GBP 0.0348/hr**, exactly as planned — the planner's m1.large default was overridden to
  flavor_id `2`. **Memory: 11.6 MiB** for the container idle, 413 MB used VM-wide of 1967 MB.
  Verified genuinely on Postgres, not the SQLite fallback (`/var/opt/memos` empty). Registration
  closed at boot by the provisioning file, admin claimed immediately afterwards, `needsSetup:false`
  and a second anonymous signup refused with 403. `MEMOS_INSTANCE_URL` set to the public hostname
  at the user's explicit choice; `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml` return 200, a PRIVATE memo returns
  401 anonymously. Write path checked end to end by creating and deleting a memo.

# Self-host Memos on redu

A fast, private place for notes and short posts: one small Go container, a managed Postgres beside
it, a public HTTPS URL. The cheapest entry in this library, at roughly GBP 25 a month.

## What this deploys

- **Memos** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.small VM, port 5230.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so your notes survive every redeploy.
- A volume on `/var/opt/memos`, which holds your attachments.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.035/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Memos on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## One decision to make before you deploy

**Private, or publicly readable?** Memos decides this with a single variable, and it swings both
ways:

- **Leave `MEMOS_INSTANCE_URL` unset** and the instance is private. RSS, the sitemap,
  `robots.txt` and anonymous attachment links all stop working.
- **Set it** and RSS and public links work, but every memo you mark PUBLIC becomes readable by
  anyone, and a sitemap listing them is served.

Neither is wrong. They are different products. Decide before you deploy rather than discovering
it afterwards.

Worth knowing, since "publicly readable" sounds worse than it is: public mode exposes only the
memos you explicitly mark PUBLIC. Measured on deploy #428, a PRIVATE memo fetched anonymously
still returned 401.

## The three that actually break it

**The signup race.** The first account created becomes the admin, and registration is open by
default, with no setup lock. Between the container going healthy and you signing up, whoever
finds the URL owns the instance. The recipe closes registration with a provisioning file before
the hostname resolves — **but deploy #428 measured that this is not sufficient on its own.** While
no admin exists, the first-account path bypasses the registration lock: an anonymous
`POST /api/v1/users` still succeeded and came back with `"role":"ADMIN"`. The identical call after
an admin existed was refused with `403 user registration is not allowed`. So the file protects the
second account onward. **You still have to claim the admin seat immediately**, then confirm
`needsSetup:false` before handing the URL to anyone.

**The driver.** Without `MEMOS_DRIVER=postgres` it quietly uses SQLite inside the container. It
comes up healthy and loses everything on the next redeploy. One command proves which one you got:
`docker exec <container> ls -la /var/opt/memos/` must be empty. A `memos_prod.db` sitting there is
the fallback.

**The volume.** Even with Postgres wired correctly, attachments still go to local disk. Postgres
keeps your notes; without a volume the files attached to them vanish.

## Deploy log

- 2026-08-16 deploy #428: ready, https://memos-q7v4m2xk.redu.cloud. **~3m50s** from the
  `deploy_compose` call to the first HTTP 200 on `/healthz`; the compose phase itself was **76s**
  (image pull, volume create, container start). m1.small app VM + managed Postgres m1.small,
  **GBP 0.0348/hr**, exactly as planned — the planner's m1.large default was overridden to
  flavor_id `2`. **Memory: 11.6 MiB** for the container idle, 413 MB used VM-wide of 1967 MB.
  Verified genuinely on Postgres, not the SQLite fallback (`/var/opt/memos` empty). Registration
  closed at boot by the provisioning file, admin claimed immediately afterwards, `needsSetup:false`
  and a second anonymous signup refused with 403. `MEMOS_INSTANCE_URL` set to the public hostname
  at the user's explicit choice; `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml` return 200, a PRIVATE memo returns
  401 anonymously. Write path checked end to end by creating and deleting a memo.

# Session report — deploying Memos on redu, and tearing it down

**Date:** 2026-08-17 (deploy events stamped 2026-08-16 UTC)
**Task as given:** *"Read redu.md and deploy Memos on redu."* — followed by *"write a report on everything
you done in this session (.md). Destroy this deployment."*
**Outcome:** Deployed, verified end to end, recorded what it taught back into `redu.md`, then destroyed.
**One resource deliberately left alive:** managed Postgres **db #131** — see [Outstanding](#outstanding--one-billed-resource-still-running).

---

## 1. Summary

Memos v0.30.0 was deployed to redu.cloud from a locally authored one-service compose stack, backed by a
redu-managed PostgreSQL on its own private VM, and reached a healthy public HTTPS endpoint in **~3m50s**.
It was verified against the failure modes `redu.md` warns about — not just "the status says ready" — then
deleted at your request.

The run produced one finding that **materially corrects the recipe**: the provisioning file that closes
signup does *not* close the first-admin race. Details in [§6](#6-findings).

| | |
|---|---|
| Deployment id | 428 (`memos`) |
| URL (while live) | `https://memos-q7v4m2xk.redu.cloud` |
| App VM | m1.small — 1 vCPU / 2 GB — `34ebc6c6-2530-41e4-b4fb-ebb104e540c5` |
| Database | managed Postgres `db-memos` (db #131), private-network only |
| Image | `neosmemo/memos:0.30.0` (pinned) |
| Cost while running | GBP 0.0348/hr (~GBP 25.40/mo) |
| Live for | roughly 10 minutes |
| Status now | **deleted** — public URL returns no connection |

---

## 2. What I did, in order

| # | Step | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Read `redu.md` | 18 recorded quirks; deploy recipe; one decision reserved for the user |
| 2 | `check_deploy_prerequisites` | ready; auto-selected network + keypair `redu-deploy-test`; guided mode |
| 3 | Authored `docker-compose.yml` + `memos-instance-setting-general.json` | one service, pinned image, volume, provisioning file |
| 4 | `plan_deploy` (pasting `redu.md` + the compose file) | costed plan + 4 preflight items; **sized m1.large — overridden** |
| 5 | Wrote `redu-deploy-plan.md` | mandatory plan artifact |
| 6 | **Asked you two questions** | private vs public; approval to spend |
| 7 | `prepare_upload` → tar + curl | 7044 bytes; upload echoed 7044 back (verified match) |
| 8 | `deploy_compose` | deployment #428 created |
| 9 | Polled `/healthz` in background | HTTP 200 after ~230s |
| 10 | Verified 9 separate properties | see [§5](#5-verification) |
| 11 | `get_deployment` with `redu_md` | server-side merge, returned `in_place` |
| 12 | Rewrote `redu.md` + `redu-deploy-plan.md` | added 8 new quirks the merge won't write itself |
| 13 | `delete_deployment(428)` | deleted; managed DB deliberately retained |

---

## 3. The two decisions

### Decision put to you: private, or publicly readable?

`redu.md` flags `MEMOS_INSTANCE_URL` as a "two-way trap" and explicitly says to ask rather than guess,
because it silently changes what the product *is*. You chose **publicly readable**, so it was set to the
deployed hostname.

A consequence worth restating: because the value must be baked in *before* the container starts, the
hostname had to be known in advance. So I generated the full `<label>-<8 chars>.redu.cloud` form myself
(`memos-q7v4m2xk.redu.cloud`) and passed it as `dname`, rather than letting redu auto-generate one and
discovering it afterwards. A bare `memos.redu.cloud` would have had a random suffix appended and would
*not* have matched what was wired in.

### Decision I made: overriding the planner's VM size

`plan_deploy` sized the app VM at **m1.large**, quoting **GBP 0.066/hr (GBP 48.18/mo)**. That floor exists
so an on-VM *build* doesn't get OOM-killed — reasonable in general, wrong here: nothing is built on this
VM, it is a pinned image pull of a statically linked Go binary. `redu.md` records m1.small as the size
that actually ran, and the planner's own preflight raised the conflict (`flavor-differs-from-record`)
without resolving it.

I deployed **m1.small** and quoted you **GBP 0.0348/hr (GBP 25.40/mo)** — the real number.
Measured idle memory afterwards was **11.6 MiB**, which settles it: m1.small was not merely adequate, it
was roomy. Following the planner would have cost **~90% more** for no benefit.

---

## 4. How the traps in `redu.md` were handled

| Trap | Handling | Confirmed how |
|---|---|---|
| `:latest` doesn't exist on Docker Hub | pinned `neosmemo/memos:0.30.0` | image pulled cleanly |
| Silent SQLite fallback | `MEMOS_DRIVER=postgres` + hand-built DSN | `/var/opt/memos` empty — no `memos_prod.db` |
| PG vars not read individually | DSN composed from `${PGUSER}`/`${PGPASSWORD}`/`${PGHOST}`/`${PGPORT}`/`${PGDATABASE}` | app connected and migrated |
| Unstated TLS mode | explicit `?sslmode=require` | read back from container env |
| Attachments lost despite Postgres | named volume → `/var/opt/memos` | mount verified rw |
| Signup race | provisioning file mounted read-only + admin claimed immediately | see [§6](#6-findings) |
| Wrong port | 5230 from image env, not the binary's 8081 | health probe passed |
| `MEMOS_MODE` is fiction | not set | — |
| SSRF via webhooks | `MEMOS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_WEBHOOKS=false`, `MEMOS_DEMO=false` | read back from container env |
| Migrations | none passed — app self-migrates | fresh DB migrated during the 76s compose phase |

---

## 5. Verification

Deliberately tested rather than inferred from a green status:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Time to first HTTP 200 on `/healthz` | ~3m50s end to end; compose phase itself 76s |
| Genuinely on Postgres, not SQLite | ✅ `/var/opt/memos` empty |
| DSN target | `postgres://<redacted>@[ip]:5432/app?sslmode=require` (private IP) |
| Attachment volume | ✅ `app-src_memos-data` → `/var/opt/memos`, rw |
| Provisioning file | ✅ mounted read-only at `/etc/secrets/…` |
| Registration closed | ✅ `disallowUserRegistration: true` |
| Second anonymous signup | ✅ refused — `403 user registration is not allowed` |
| Admin seat | ✅ claimed; `needsSetup: false`; signin returns a token |
| Public mode | ✅ `robots.txt` + `sitemap.xml` → 200 |
| Private memo, anonymous | ✅ `401` — public mode exposes only what's marked PUBLIC |
| Write path end to end | ✅ memo created, then deleted |
| Container memory, idle | 11.6 MiB (0.59% of 1.922 GiB); VM 413 MB of 1967 MB |

---

## 6. Findings

### 6.1 The provisioning file does not close the admin race — the headline

`redu.md` said mounting the provisioning file closes registration "before the hostname is ever reachable",
implying the instance is safe to leave sitting. **Measured: it isn't.**

With the file mounted and the API correctly reporting `disallowUserRegistration: true`, an **anonymous**
`POST /api/v1/users` still returned **200** with `"role":"ADMIN"` — because `needsSetup` was still `true`
and no host user existed. The identical request *after* an admin existed was refused with
`403 user registration is not allowed`.

So the flag protects the **second account onward, not the first**. The race window stays open from the
moment the hostname resolves until somebody claims the admin seat. That is why I claimed it during
verification instead of handing over an unclaimed URL. Recorded in `redu.md` as a ⛔⛔⛔ quirk that
explicitly corrects the two quirks above it.

### 6.2 v0.30.0 renamed the API surface; older paths 404

Cost a round of guessing, so it is now recorded:

| Purpose | v0.30.0 path | What 404s |
|---|---|---|
| First admin / signup | `POST /api/v1/users` | `/api/v1/auth/signup`, `/api/v1/auth/register` |
| Login | `POST /api/v1/auth/signin` with `{"passwordCredentials":{…}}` | `/[REDACTED:value]`, `/api/v1/auth/sessions` |
| Instance state | `GET /api/v1/instance/profile` | `/api/v1/workspace/profile` |
| Settings | `GET /api/v1/instance/settings/GENERAL` | — |

The `workspace` → `instance` rename is why every older tutorial's path fails.

### 6.3 A memory number, where upstream publishes none

**11.6 MiB** idle for the container; **413 MB of 1967 MB** VM-wide including Ubuntu, dockerd and
containerd. `redu.md` previously carried only a hedge ("m1.small is a reasonable floor"). The media
caveat still stands — the 30 MB per-upload limit and server-side thumbnail/motion transcoding are what
actually move memory — but nobody should be talked up a size for a text notebook.

### 6.4 The `redu.md` merge silently skips new quirks

`get_deployment` returned `redu_md_merge_mode: "in_place"` because the file is richer than redu's
template. In-place refreshes `last_deploy` and appends one deploy-log line — but **does not write new
quirks**. An agent that trusts the merge blindly loses everything its run learned. Now recorded as a
quirk, so the next run knows to hand-add.

### 6.5 Minor

- The alpine image ships **busybox wget, not curl** — so a container healthcheck must use `wget`. It
  reported `(healthy)`.
- The upload's `size_bytes` echo (7044) was checked against the local tarball size, per `prepare_upload`'s
  own warning about stale uploads.

---

## 7. Files in `/home/milos/Desktop/tests_lib/memos/`

| File | Status | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `redu.md` | **modified** | server-merged, **+8 new quirks** from this run, deploy log entry with measured figures |
| `redu-deploy-plan.md` | **created** | real deployed values + verification table (replaced the pre-deploy estimate) |
| `docker-compose.yml` | **created** | the deployed stack |
| `memos-instance-setting-general.json` | **created** | provisioning file that closes registration at boot |
| `SESSION-REPORT.md` | **created** | this report |

No credentials were written to any file. The admin password was handed over in the session only, per
`redu.md`'s ⛔ instruction — and is moot now that the instance is destroyed.

---

## 8. Teardown

`delete_deployment(428)` — deployment and app VM destroyed, confirmed two ways: gone from
`list_deployments`, and the public URL now fails to connect (curl `000`).

The app VM's volume went with it. That volume held attachments; none had been uploaded, and the one test
memo had already been deleted.

The unrelated `postiz` deployment (#427) on the same account was left untouched.

### Outstanding — one billed resource still running

`delete_deployment` **never** deletes the managed database, by design, so notes survive a redeploy:

> **managed Postgres db #131** (VM `db-memos`) — still running, still billing at **GBP 0.0174/hr**
> (~GBP 12.70/mo). It contains only the `admin` account created during verification.

I did not delete it, because that is irreversible and "destroy this deployment" names the deployment, not
the database. **To remove it and stop that charge: `delete_database(131)`** — say the word and I will.

---

## 9. Cost

While live: **GBP 0.0348/hr** across both VMs, for roughly 10 minutes. Billing is hourly, so expect at
most about **GBP 0.035** for the app VM's hour. The retained database continues at GBP 0.0174/hr until
deleted.

`POST /api/v1/users` still returned **200** with `"role":"ADMIN"` — because `needsSetup` was still `true`
and no host user existed. The identical request *after* an admin existed was refused with
`403 user registration is not allowed`.

So the flag protects the **second account onward, not the first**. The race window stays open from the
moment the hostname resolves until somebody claims the admin seat. That is why I claimed it during
verification instead of handing over an unclaimed URL. Recorded in `redu.md` as a ⛔⛔⛔ quirk that
explicitly corrects the two quirks above it.

### 6.2 v0.30.0 renamed the API surface; older paths 404

Cost a round of guessing, so it is now recorded:

| Purpose | v0.30.0 path | What 404s |
|---|---|---|
| First admin / signup | `POST /api/v1/users` | `/api/v1/auth/signup`, `/api/v1/auth/register` |
| Login | `POST /api/v1/auth/signin` with `{"passwordCredentials":{…}}` | `/[REDACTED:value]`, `/api/v1/auth/sessions` |
| Instance state | `GET /api/v1/instance/profile` | `/api/v1/workspace/profile` |
| Settings | `GET /api/v1/instance/settings/GENERAL` | — |

The `workspace` → `instance` rename is why every older tutorial's path fails.

### 6.3 A memory number, where upstream publishes none

**11.6 MiB** idle for the container; **413 MB of 1967 MB** VM-wide including Ubuntu, dockerd and
containerd. `redu.md` previously carried only a hedge ("m1.small is a reasonable floor"). The media
caveat still stands — the 30 MB per-upload limit and server-side thumbnail/motion transcoding are what
actually move memory — but nobody should be talked up a size for a text notebook.

### 6.4 The `redu.md` merge silently skips new quirks

`get_deployment` returned `redu_md_merge_mode: "in_place"` because the file is richer than redu's
template. In-place refreshes `last_deploy` and appends one deploy-log line — but **does not write new
quirks**. An agent that trusts the merge blindly loses everything its run learned. Now recorded as a
quirk, so the next run knows to hand-add.

### 6.5 Minor

- The alpine image ships **busybox wget, not curl** — so a container healthcheck must use `wget`. It
  reported `(healthy)`.
- The upload's `size_bytes` echo (7044) was checked against the local tarball size, per `prepare_upload`'s
  own warning about stale uploads.

| File | Status | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `redu.md` | **modified** | server-merged, **+8 new quirks** from this run, deploy log entry with measured figures |
| `redu-deploy-plan.md` | **created** | real deployed values + verification table (replaced the pre-deploy estimate) |
| `docker-compose.yml` | **created** | the deployed stack |
| `memos-instance-setting-general.json` | **created** | provisioning file that closes registration at boot |
| `SESSION-REPORT.md` | **created** | this report |

No credentials were written to any file. The admin password was handed over in the session only, per
`redu.md`'s ⛔ instruction — and is moot now that the instance is destroyed.

---

## 8. Teardown

`delete_deployment(428)` — deployment and app VM destroyed, confirmed two ways: gone from
`list_deployments`, and the public URL now fails to connect (curl `000`).

The app VM's volume went with it. That volume held attachments; none had been uploaded, and the one test
memo had already been deleted.

The unrelated `postiz` deployment (#427) on the same account was left untouched.

### Outstanding — one billed resource still running

`delete_deployment` **never** deletes the managed database, by design, so notes survive a redeploy:

> **managed Postgres db #131** (VM `db-memos`) — still running, still billing at **GBP 0.0174/hr**
> (~GBP 12.70/mo). It contains only the `admin` account created during verification.

I did not delete it, because that is irreversible and "destroy this deployment" names the deployment, not
the database. **To remove it and stop that charge: `delete_database(131)`** — say the word and I will.

While live: **GBP 0.0348/hr** across both VMs, for roughly 10 minutes. Billing is hourly, so expect at
most about **GBP 0.035** for the app VM's hour. The retained database continues at GBP 0.0174/hr until
deleted.
